handback.t:
R6-A (h13) DONE. Nothing in src/ was touched, nothing was committed, nothing was downloaded. Everything is synthetic-until-validated: real text, but simulated agents and outcomes. Full write-up: C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\h13_board_entry.md. Proposed patch: results\h13_proposed_patch.md. Lessons: results\lessons_h13.md.

**Decision**
- **Retrieval quality: yes.** Hybrid z-score (alpha .7) plus spell should replace dense+spell as the recommended opt-in retrieval on real documentation text.
  - The gain replicates in two independent text worlds.
  - Net cost is about +1.4% query compute (+23 us) and +10% index bytes, with no extra model call.
- **Routing success: no.** End-to-end, every spell-corrected variant ties dense+spell, with 0 Holm differences. The largest gap is |d| ≤ .009, over 8 worlds × 3 splits × 3 gates.
- **Rejected:** RRF, RSF and rerank-20. Spell stays a separate switch.
- **Gate:** keep the g16 safe gate, defaults unchanged. On real text the ungated g1 gate gave 2-3x the gain of the safe gate without harming the one-off control, so g16's "gate is required" did not replicate here.

**Doc-level retrieval** (A held 31-60 / A confirm 61-90 / B confirm 61-90; 126 Holm tests per split; "robust" = Holm-significant under both the seed t-test and a query-cluster bootstrap)
- Hybrid z+spell minus dense+spell, MRR: +.040 / +.048 / +.028, robust in all three.
  - hit@1 and F1@3 gains are robust only in A. In B they fail the bootstrap Holm.
- RRF is .018-.024 MRR worse than z-fusion in all three splits.
- RSF is +.034 / +.041 / +.024 over dense, but not distinguishable from z.
- Rerank-20 matches z-fusion in A (+.042 / +.049 over dense) but does not replicate in B (+.007, n.s.). Its beta was tuned on A.
- Spell adds +.015 MRR; it costs -.002 on clean queries.
- BM25 alone ties dense in A and is worse in B (-.022, n.s. after Holm).
- Other tables:
  - P/R/F1 @1/3/5, hit@1/MRR and the seed-t and bootstrap CIs are in `results/h13_retrieval.json`; the key tables are in `results/h13_summary.txt`.
  - Latency/bytes, for 6,831 docs (single thread, brute-force scan, live compute, per query; excludes the 3-8 ms MiniLM encode and the spell corrector):

| Variant | Total per query |
|---|---|
| Dense (incl. top-8) | 1641 us |
| Hybrid z | ~1664 us |
| RRF | 1694 us |
| RSF | 1706 us |
| Rerank-20 | 1698 us |

  - Dense vectors are 10.49 MB; the BM25 index is 1.03 MB.

**End-to-end routing** (g16 loop: top-1 paragraph, topic-cluster anchor vote, safe gate; tuned on A seeds 1-8, frozen on A 61-90 and B 61-90; context helps only if the injected paragraph is structurally relevant)
- Versus the same-gate dense+spell arm: 0 Holm wins and 0 losses for bm25_s, hybz_s, hybrrf_s, hybrsf_s and rerank_s in every world and split.
  - The only losses in the whole table are no-spell variants.
- Only the oracle (a relevant paragraph always) wins: +.22 over the same gate.
  - Real retrieval captures about 4% of that gain under the safe gate and about 9% under the g1 gate.
  - Injected-paragraph precision is only .17-.24, so a +.03 hit@1 gain is worth about +.001 H2000.
- Topic-dependent worlds (T12, T12-drift, T48, T12-noctx), H2000 versus the guarded front without retrieval (T12 level .5875 in A held):
  - Safe gate: -.002 to +.010, Holm wins in only 2 cells, none in B.
  - g1 gate: +.02 to +.027 in A (Holm wins in all four worlds); in B +.014 to +.015 in T12, T12-drift and T12-noctx, and n.s. in T48 (+.004).
- Controls:
  - **ctl-oneoff (source absent from the store):** the safe arms are TOST-equivalent to the front within ±.01 in all 3 splits. The g1 arms are +.002 to +.014.
  - **ctl-irrel (topic-independent, context useless):** arms sit 0.15 *below* a plain global Thompson bandit that I added post-hoc, so wins versus the front in the topic-independent worlds are front-learning-speed artifacts, not retrieval value.
- Post-hoc and untuned: in a context-essential world (Tqa), hybrid minus dense is +.017 in A held and +.013 in B confirm, Holm-significant. The oracle there is .88 against about .33 for real retrieval.

**g1 vs h10 discrepancy: a corpus-property effect, supported by statistics but not proven by an intervention**
- Same engine on the g1 templated corpora: hybrid MRR is only +.013 in A and +.008 (n.s.) in B. F1@3 drops .624 → .550, and RRF is a Holm loss in B.
- g1 has no headroom: dense hit@1 is .92, against .20 on real text. On real text, 80% of queries have a non-relevant paragraph closer than the relevant one.
- g1's relevance pair is deliberately paraphrased, so the lexical leg hurts the second relevant document. g1 has an 805-word vocabulary with 0% hapax terms; real text has 10.9k words, 40% hapax.
- Raw lexical overlap does not explain it: g1 queries overlap their documents more (.565) than real ones (.34).
- Inside real text, hybrid gain follows overlap by tertile: A -.035 / +.042 / +.127, B -.028 / +.030 / +.079. In the lowest-overlap third, hybrid loses.

**Caveats and post-hoc changes (all disclosed in the board entry)**
- Added after the first runs: the top-k vote parameter, the ctx-only gate, the Tqa world and the global-ts baseline. Tuned picks are unchanged by the baseline addition; the pre-change outputs are kept as `results/h13_route_v1_6baselines.*`.
- Tuned admission floors sit at the grid edge, and a wider grid was not tried.
- Routing has no query-cluster bootstrap; the A→B replication is the independence check.
- B has fewer queries (1,029), so its CIs are wider.
- Relevance is structural (section or source-paragraph membership), not human-rated.
- The top-lists were replayed from a cache; a live pipeline would add the embedding latency per task.

**Reproducibility:** a repeat reproduced `h13_retrieval.json` and `h13_route.json` bit-for-bit except for timing fields. The top-list files (`h13_top_*.bin`) and `h13_picks.json` are md5-identical.
